verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never writes this inequality out; it encodes the same class membership as a weighted-jet predicate, and that predicate is exactly the shape of the forcing hypothesis hf : LocalJets s (fun n x => Real.sqrt (s.zeta x) * W n x) alpha cells (fun n _ => source n) of ParticularCopyBounds.coefficients_jets (line 246). The rewriting has four parts. (i) Degrees: the paper carries two exponents, S_*^{b_I} and delta^{-a_I}; majorant carries one common degree p on growth n x = S_n * max 1 (delta x)⁻¹. The two are interchangeable, and the repository says so: WeightedClasses.MemClass.of_separate_bounds (line 147) converts separate S and inverse-edge-distance degrees into the common p = b + a, and a common p is the case b = a = p. (ii) max 1 (delta x)⁻¹ equals delta(x)⁻¹ wherever delta(x) ≤ 1, and is the larger of the two otherwise, so the Lean weight dominates the paper's. (iii) The envelope P(v) of (7.12) appears as an abstract weight factor W n x, tied to the transported envelope by a hypothesis envelope ≤ W; the same W appears in hypothesis and conclusion, so this is a change of majorant, not of content. (iv) D^I for one multi-index is replaced by the full ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j‖ for every j ≤ m, which bounds all multi-indices of order j. C and p are existentially quantified per differentiation order, matching the paper's C_I, b_I, a_I depending on I.
